entries.target: wine:Mas de Valériole ‘Vé’ Rosé Méditerranée 2025 (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: Mas de Valériole Vé Rosé Méditerranée 2025, in magnum, is a pale, dry rosé from a family estate in the Camargue, the Rhône delta south of Arles. It blends Caladoc, a cross of Grenache and Malbec, with Merlot and Marselan, pressed straight off the skins and kept fresh in steel: raspberry, ripe citrus and a salty, sea breeze finish. Two bottles in one, it suits a big table sharing crab, tomato and crisp salads in the courtyard. It goes on ice the moment it is ordered, and we pour it at 45 to 48°F in a white wine glass. Vé is a Provençal expression meaning look at that.

entries.target: wine:Pierre Péters ‘Cuvée de Réserve’ Brut NV (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: Pierre Péters Cuvée de Réserve Brut, in magnum, is grower Champagne from Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, a Grand Cru village of the Côte des Blancs. It is all Grand Cru Chardonnay, mainly Le Mesnil with Oger, Cramant and Avize, blended with a perpetual reserve of older wines and aged at least two years on its lees: lemon, white flowers, chalk and a creamy, fine mousse. It suits a table sharing oysters and crab. We chill it well, serve it at 45 to 48°F in a tulip, and hold the bigger cork and cage firmly. The first Pierre Péters label came out in 1946, the year Brennan’s opened.

entries.target: wine:Jean Foillard ‘Côte du Py’ Morgon 2023 (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: Jean Foillard Côte du Py Morgon 2023, in magnum, is Gamay from old vines on the Côte du Py, the schist hill at the heart of Morgon, a Beaujolais cru. Made with whole bunches, native yeasts and little sulphur, then aged in old Burgundy barrels, it gives dark cherry, raspberry, violet and an earthy depth, with silky tannin and lively acidity. Light enough for fish and deep enough for duck, mushrooms or cheese, it suits a table of mixed plates. We serve it slightly cool, 55 to 58°F, in a Burgundy bowl. The Gang of Four of Morgon followed the oenologist Jules Chauvet back to these old ways.

entries.target: wine:Duckhorn Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022 (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: Duckhorn Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 2022, in magnum, is Cabernet Sauvignon drawn from vineyards across the Napa Valley and aged in French oak. It tastes of blackcurrant, black cherry, cocoa and a little cedar, ripe and polished, with firm but rounded tannin. Protein and fat soften that tannin, so it suits a party sharing steak and roast beef, two bottles in one. We serve it at 60 to 64°F in a large Bordeaux glass; a young magnum opens with air, so we offer to decant it at the side stand. Duckhorn, founded in 1976, made its name with Merlot when few in America took the grape seriously.

entries.target: wine:Château Cos d’Estournel Saint-Estèphe 2015 (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: Château Cos d’Estournel Saint-Estèphe 2015, in magnum, is a Second Growth of the 1855 classification, on a gravel ridge facing Lafite across the Pauillac boundary. It is Cabernet Sauvignon blended with Merlot and bottled here in magnum, which ages more slowly: blackcurrant, plum, cedar, cocoa and exotic spice, powerful and polished, with firm, fine tannin and a long finish. It is made for a beef celebration. We stand the magnum upright, decant it off its sediment at the side stand an hour ahead, and serve it at 62 to 65°F. Its founder, Louis Gaspard d’Estournel, sold his wine into India and built pagodas to say so.

entries.target: wine:J.J. Prüm ‘Wehlener Sonnenuhr’ Riesling Auslese Goldkapsel 2015 (1.5 L magnum)
entries.value: J.J. Prüm Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Auslese Goldkapsel 2015, in magnum, is sweet Riesling from the steep slate of the Wehlener Sonnenuhr at Wehlen, on the Mosel. Auslese means selected bunches, and the gold capsule marks a richer selection: honeyed pineapple, apricot, lime and slate, sweet and racy, light in alcohol. As our celebration bottle for the Pineapple Tarte Tatin, its pineapple meets the charred fruit and its acidity keeps the anglaise light. We pour 2 to 3 oz at 45 to 50°F in small dessert glasses, about twenty from the magnum. In 1842 Jodocus Prüm built the sundial into the slate, and the vineyard took its name.

entries.target: wine:Les Cadrans de Lassègue Saint-Émilion Grand Cru 2021
entries.value: Les Cadrans de Lassègue Saint-Émilion Grand Cru 2021 is the second wine of Château Lassègue, on Bordeaux’s Right Bank, first made in 2008 from the estate’s younger vines and foothill blocks. Mainly Merlot with Cabernet Franc, it spends six to eight months in French oak and tastes of red cherry, plum and a little spice, with soft, refined tannin and a fresh finish. As our value bottle for the Chateau Espagnole, that soft tannin suits the lean Chateaubriand and its plum and spice meet the brown sauce. We serve it at 60 to 64°F in a Bordeaux glass, no decanting. Cadrans are the sundials on the château’s front.
